title: Deterministic fracture model
problem: Cards have no reproducible crack and mend geometry, so shared seeds cannot reconstruct a visitor's gold seams.
action_items: Define stable eligible card IDs and deterministic seeded branching fracture paths from normalized click coordinates, with bounded path count and SVG dimensions.
Create pure gesture classification for clustered pointerdowns and shake thresholds; define reduced-motion behavior and test branch geometry, seed replay, limits, gesture timing, and malformed inputs.
Record task evidence with executable/build identity, real versus fixture boundary, test outcomes, and any deferred external check.
acceptance_criteria: The same card, seed and origin reproduce the same bounded fracture and gold seam paths; clustered clicks and supported shake thresholds classify deterministically, including a reduced-motion bypass.

title: Shared seam store and API
problem: Repaired seams disappear on reload and unrestricted writes could inflate rankings or grow storage.
action_items: Read the installed Next route handler guide, add Drizzle schema and migration for aggregate card counts, capped recent seam seeds, and bounded usage buckets.
Implement transactional admit/list/top operations using an allowlist, hashed visitor bucket, per-card and hourly limits, daily global cap, and bounded cleanup; do not persist raw identifiers.

Expose POST and GET /api/kintsugi with validated payloads, safe error codes, no-cache write responses and graceful read fallback; add store/API tests with a real throwaway Postgres fixture or equivalent transaction integration fixture and rejection controls.

At task start, if a new DB capability or permission absent from the declared prerequisites is discovered and only an operator can establish it, raise an exact prerequisite-linked operator_action; proceed with independent implementation.
Record task evidence with executable/build identity, real versus fixture boundary, test outcomes, and any deferred external check.
acceptance_criteria: A valid card mend is stored and returned with bounded shared seeds and counts; invalid IDs, duplicate or over-limit visitors, and exhausted global budget cannot write. Database outage produces a bounded service response without exposing identifiers.

title: Kintsugi card interaction
problem: Visitors cannot discover or experience the crack-and-gold repair on existing page cards.
action_items: Read installed Next client/layout guidance; mount one lightweight Kintsugi layer and opt stable existing cards in with data-kintsugi IDs.
Recognize clustered pointer clicks and permission-gated DeviceMotion after a gesture; keep interactive card DOM and focus order intact, with decorative SVG aria-hidden and pointer-events none.

Animate origin-based ink fracture, restrained displacement, paper-crunch via the existing off-by-default Web Audio gate, then gold dash reveal and sheen; reduced motion skips drift/shake and fades seams in.

Send a bounded mend request, replay stored seeds, and leave local repair usable when offline or rate-limited. Add browser tests for click, supported motion, mute, card link, API failure and reduced motion.
Record task evidence with executable/build identity, real versus fixture boundary, test outcomes, and any deferred external check.
acceptance_criteria: Four near clicks crack an opted-in card from the clicked point and mend it in gold; the card remains usable, sound honors the site switch, stored seams replay, and reduced motion is calm. Shake works only after supported permission.

title: Activity event model and export
problem: The daily ledger lacks event timestamps and job size data required for an honest strip-chart trace.
action_items: Define and validate a versioned event schema for individual public commits, PRs and pipeline runs with safe short labels, status, runtime and row counts; add a checked-in pipeline export fixture and nonempty seismo.json.
Build a fail-soft GitHub refresh script modeled on ledger-fetch that retains the last valid trace on API failure or rate limit and never emits token, private body, logs or raw sensitive metadata.

Implement pure log-scaled magnitude, failure blot classification, stable time ordering, viewport/downsampling and SVG geometry/export helpers; test malformed feeds, outliers, duplicate events, rate-limit fallback and nonempty static output.
Record task evidence with executable/build identity, real versus fixture boundary, test outcomes, and any deferred external check.
non_goals: live GitHub request from the browser
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in, timestamped, validated activity feed yields deterministic bounded tremors and failed-run blots; refresh preserves the last valid trace when GitHub fails, and the feed contains no credentials or private bodies.

title: Work page ink seismograph
problem: The Work page has no paper recorder, event inspection or shareable strip, and cannot rely on JavaScript for its initial data.
action_items: Read installed Next server/client guidance; add a server-rendered SVG trace and named event list driven by the checked-in feed on the Work page, preserving meaningful no-JS content.
Enhance with a bounded-DPR canvas ink trace, subtle wobble and bleed, red failure blots, viewport/visibility-paused animation and reduced-motion stationary mode.
Implement pointer-drag and keyboard/range scrubbing, tappable spike details, and a tear-off standalone SVG download with torn edge and print stylesheet; keep a visible timeline and accessible labels.
Test real fixture spike selection, drag/keyboard window changes, failure blot, nonempty SVG download/print, no-JS SSR, hidden tab and reduced-motion behavior in browser.
Record task evidence with executable/build identity, real versus fixture boundary, test outcomes, and any deferred external check.
non_goals: changing existing Work content outside the recorder
acceptance_criteria: Work shows a real static chart and event list without JavaScript; with JavaScript, visitors can inspect and scrub spikes, see failed runs in red, and download a nonempty printable SVG of the selected window. Reduced motion is stationary.
